pitfalls.problem: build_gantt.py opened with a single-quoted multi-line string, so importing it from build_matrices.py raised SyntaxError and the 'Build matrices from authority files' step exited 1 (run 42553625095).
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trusting the write_file ok=true receipt as proof the Python source parses; the receipt proves the blob landed, not that it is valid Python.
pitfalls.lesson: A new module imported by build_matrices must start with a real docstring or comment, and its first proof is the build step conclusion on the following push run - not the write receipt.
pitfalls.resolution: Docstring edit at 96ef7894 produced green run 42554257008.

pitfalls.problem: 'Commit regenerated matrices' exited 1 at 42553597443, which I initially attributed to an unguarded commit on a clean tree.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Diagnosing the failing step from its name instead of reading the step body; the workflow at 3fc6c647 already wraps commit/push in an `if git diff --cached --quiet` guard.
pitfalls.lesson: Read the workflow step body before proposing a workflow repair. When the guard is already present, a step-7 exit 1 means the else-branch ran and the commit or push itself failed, so look at tree state and remote head at that commit rather than rewriting the guard.
pitfalls.correction: Misdiagnosis corrected; no workflow change required for this id.

pitfalls.problem: Unauthenticated job pages return 'This step has been truncated due to its large size' for every step, so the failing log line is never visible.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trying to read the cause from the job HTML page.
pitfalls.lesson: Use run_jobs step conclusions plus the annotation list (which names the step and 'Process completed with exit code 1'); never quote a log line that was not actually returned.

pitfalls.problem: The workflow's own 'Commit regenerated matrices' step pushed 187168f5, so the branch head no longer matched the sha my prior read/plan assumed.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Assuming branch_head stays at the last file I wrote; a push-triggered run on this branch rewrites the matrices and pushes a new head.
pitfalls.lesson: Before any write, take branch_head and read the target file at that head; expected_sha must come from that same read, and the post-push head will be one or more commits ahead of my write.
